name: Cows
label: AmRep
lede: A Minneapolis band that treated a bugle as a lead instrument and its singer's costume drawer as a weapon, and made some of the most gleefully hostile records on [[Amphetamine Reptile Records]].

eras.title: Steel wool and a new singer
eras.text: Cows start in Minneapolis in the mid-1980s, lose their first vocalist within months, and find Shannon Selberg, who turns a rehearsal-room racket into a stage act.

years.h: Two brothers, a guitarist and a drummer start a band
years.p: [[Kevin Rutmanis|140e4f42-ff95-470b-af7b-bd4be6e96db7]] and his brother Sandris Rutmanis form Cows in Minneapolis with guitarist [[Thor Eisentrager|470a21c4-785a-473a-8b0c-01a0d33156aa]] and drummer [[Norm Rogers|49f6514a-d4e8-4383-8099-56062daf16c4]]. Wikipedia dates the start to 1986; other sources say late 1985.

years.h: Shannon Selberg takes the mic, Norm Rogers goes to the Jayhawks
years.p: Rogers leaves in January 1987 to drum for The Jayhawks, and [[Shannon Selberg|f032b603-a6dd-4349-ab47-53ebefc04667]] joins in February as frontman on vocals and bugle.

years.h: Taint Pluribus Taint Unum · Treehouse debut
years.p: The first album comes out on the Minneapolis label Treehouse. Trouser Press calls it an elementary introduction, a storm of electrified steel wool.
years.xp: The band has a fifth member in these years: David van der Steen, listed on Wikipedia as a 'fifth udder' from 1987 to 1992. Encyclopedia.com says critics at the time wrote the group off as talentless.

years.h: Tony Oliveri replaces Sandris Rutmanis on drums
years.p: [[Tony Oliveri|851fd100-d707-4064-b056-f72b124c3b7e]] takes the drum stool, and the band puts out the Chow 7-inch on Treehouse the same year.

eras.title: Signed to the reptiles
eras.text: Cows land on Tom Hazelmyer's Amphetamine Reptile Records, home of the Twin Cities' loudest, and make three records in three years.

years.h: Daddy Has a Tail! · first AmRep album
years.p: [[Tom Hazelmyer|d6569a63-5da9-41fa-a5c9-b6b11b496218]]'s label issues the second album, built partly on covers rewritten with cruder words. Thor Eisentrager's overdriven guitar is the murk everything sits in.

years.h: Effete and Impudent Snobs sharpens the noise
years.p: Trouser Press hears far more clarity and focus than on the last one, with layered guitar shards and Shannon Selberg's distorted vocals up front.
years.xp: The Slap Back 7-inch also appears on AmRep this year. They share the label with other Minneapolis-area noise bands such as [[Hammerhead|ea15533d-5ea7-4605-85d5-7634c38a6258]] and Hazelmyer's own [[Halo of Flies|3a26de45-4f41-4e28-bdc8-fda60ef0c8d0]].

years.h: Norm Rogers comes back to the drums
years.p: [[Norm Rogers|49f6514a-d4e8-4383-8099-56062daf16c4]], who left in 1987 for The Jayhawks, returns to replace Tony Oliveri and stays until 1995.

years.h: Peacetika goes chunky and stop-start
years.p: Trouser Press says the band trades twisted humor for more screaming and instrumental noise.

eras.title: The bugle era
eras.text: The middle records get better recorded and stranger. Selberg's bugle moves up front and his costumes become the story on the road.

years.h: Cunning Stunts: a spoonerism and a better-sounding record
years.p: Iain Burgess produces at Mirror Image in Minneapolis, a clear step up in sound quality from earlier albums, with Norm Rogers on drums and the bugle in the mix.
years.xp: The cover alludes to Reid Miles' design for Eric Dolphy's 1964 jazz album Out to Lunch!. City Pages later put it among AmRep's greatest albums and among the best Minneapolis albums of the 1990s. The band toured North America behind it.

years.big: Dark comedy in a stuffed-animal suit
years.src: Wikipedia · New York Times · Trouser Press · Encyclopedia.com
years.h: Shaving cream, mousetraps and stuffed animals
years.p: Shannon Selberg performs nearly naked in shaving cream, with mousetraps on his ears, and in costumes made from stuffed animals and love dolls.
years.xp:
The New York Times, reviewing them in May 1992, described the wardrobe as merging defiance, pain and dark comedy. Trouser Press also notes fake-fur football uniforms and business suits with stuffed animals, with facial features drawn on in marker.

Selberg himself has framed it plainly.

years.h: Sexy Pee Story keeps up the pressure
years.p: Trouser Press says the album widens its subject matter to betrayal in several parts of life, without letting the music ease off.

years.h: Cow Island 7-inch on AmRep
years.p: The single arrives alongside Orphan's Tragedy, which Wikipedia dates to 1994 and Trouser Press to 1995.

eras.title: New drummer, last record
eras.text: Rogers leaves, Freddy Votel steps in, Selberg moves to New York, and the band ends with a record produced by the Melvins' front man.

years.h: Freddy Votel replaces Norm Rogers
years.p: [[Freddy Votel|6340eac7-8561-4e1d-abee-6b3798cfbe55]] becomes the fourth drummer. Encyclopedia.com says the band stays together even with Selberg living in New York.

years.h: Old Gold 1989-1991 collects the early AmRep years
years.p: A compilation of material from the first stretch on the label. Wikipedia dates it 1995, Trouser Press 1996.

years.h: Whorn lets the horns lead
years.p: Trouser Press says the bugle sometimes replaces guitar as the main melodic voice.

years.h: Sorry in Pig Minor, produced by King Buzzo of the Melvins
years.p: Buzz Osborne of the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] produces the ninth and final album at AmRep Recording Division in Minneapolis (AMREP 066), running 47 minutes.
years.xp:
The closing track 'Say Uncle' runs over 13 minutes, with about five minutes of silence before a rough dub remix and more studio material. Encyclopedia.com says the record brings Latin and jazz colors into the punk.

Trouser Press calls it a prolonged symphony in adrenalized guitar wang, with bugle.

years.h: Thor Eisentrager quits touring and the band ends
years.p: According to Wikipedia, Eisentrager leaves after the ninth album citing exhaustion from touring, and the rest disband soon after. Kevin Rutmanis moves on to the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]].

eras.title: Afterlives
eras.text: Members scatter into other bands and jobs, the label and fans keep the records alive, and Norm Rogers dies in 2018.

years.h: Selberg heads to New York for The Heroine Sheiks
years.p: [[Shannon Selberg|f032b603-a6dd-4349-ab47-53ebefc04667]] moves to New York City and joins the noise-rock group The Heroine Sheiks, adding keyboards. Pitchfork called him the Crispin Glover of noise rock.

years.h: Kevin Rutmanis plays bass for the Melvins
years.p: Wikipedia lists him in the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]] from 1998 until June 2005, and on the first two Tomahawk albums, the self-titled debut and Mit Gas.

years.h: Cows and the Melvins share a Sugar Daddy Live split
years.p: The band appears on Volume 2 of the Sugar Daddy Live Split Series, paired with the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]].

years.h: Demos come out as Stunning Cunts
years.p: Two volumes of demo recordings, titled Stunning Cunts and Stunning Cunts Vol. 2, appear in 2014 and 2015.

years.h: Norm Rogers dies of cancer
years.p: The Current and the Star Tribune reported that the Cows and Jayhawks drummer died in February 2018 after a terminal cancer diagnosis; he had been a manager at Brit's Pub in Minneapolis.
years.xp: Rogers drummed on the Jayhawks' 1986 self-titled debut and on Cows' Cunning Stunts. At a farewell party at Brit's the month before, he wrote that his heart was full and that he had lived a helluva life for a lad from small-town western Minnesota.
